description: Reachability-truth confirmation taxonomy. Drives confirm_reachability.py + confirm_gate.py. The precision lever: not 'could this be a bug in theory' but 'can an UNPRIVILEGED attacker drive the claimed path to the claimed impact in the relevant deployed lifecycle state?'. Targets the eval2 residual FP classes (AR-001/DS-004/RE-001 speculative reachability; SG-004/DT-011/BSA-005 lifecycle/init misreads; OR-005 severity overclaim).
_honesty_note: Deterministic checks only DOWNGRADE or FLAG. mark_false_positive is reserved for a clear deterministic kill (dead_path / guard provably blocks). A speculative finding (public entrypoint but unproven precondition/impact) routes to uncertain + needs_runtime_poc — NEVER auto-FP and NEVER auto-confirm. We do not overclaim confirmation in either direction.

detection_hints: no affected/consumer function is external|public state-changing
external_entrypoint_missing.required_evidence: an external/public attacker-callable entrypoint that reaches the sink
external_entrypoint_missing.review_prompt_hint: Name the external entrypoint an EOA calls; if none, the finding is not attacker-reachable.
examples: a bug only in an internal helper with no public caller

detection_hints: affected fn internal/private; no public caller surfaced in manifest/ice_chain
no_call_chain_to_sink.review_prompt_hint: Trace entrypoint -> sink; if the chain can't be built, downgrade.

detection_hints: the fn or all callers carry a privileged modifier
privileged_only.required_evidence: an unprivileged caller path, OR an argument that the privileged actor is untrusted
privileged_only.review_prompt_hint: Is every path gated by onlyOwner/role/governance? If so it is not an unprivileged-attacker finding.
examples: onlyOwner setter flagged as attacker bug

detection_hints: governance/timelock modifier or caller
admin role gate
onlyOwner / Ownable
fn kind initializer OR file in reseed/init/migration; reachable only during a one-time lifecycle step
lifecycle_only.required_evidence: an in-normal-operation reachable path, OR an accepted impact for the lifecycle window
lifecycle_only.review_prompt_hint: Only reachable during reseed/init/migration (owner-gated diamondCut)? then it is not a permissionless steady-state finding.
examples: SG-004 reseed init 'no access modifier' — owner-gated via diamondCut

detection_hints: kind==initializer / name init
migration/L1/L2 file
disposition deferred_out_of_scope; zero callers; unreachable
dead_path.review_prompt_hint: Dead code with zero callers — not exploitable.

detection_hints: no caller in manifest/ice_chain; consumer_found=false; internal
zero_callers.review_prompt_hint: No caller surfaced — confirm one exists.

detection_hints: assumes a chain/deploy that doesn't hold
deployment_context_mismatch.review_prompt_hint: Does the assumed chain/deploy match the target?
examples: L1-only assumption on an L2 deploy

detection_hints: impact requires a state the invariants forbid
impossible_state.required_evidence: a path that reaches the required state
impossible_state.review_prompt_hint: Can the required precondition state actually be reached?
examples: needs ratio < 1e4 with no path shown

detection_hints: a require/guard in the path provably blocks the attacker input
guard_blocks_attack.review_prompt_hint: Does an explicit guard stop the claimed input?

detection_hints: a modifier blocks the attacker
explicit role check blocks attacker
role_check_blocks_attack.review_prompt_hint: Does a role check block it?

detection_hints: the vulnerable input is not attacker-controlled
examples: value set only by trusted oracle/keeper

detection_hints: the claimed impact does not follow from the corrupted state
impact_not_reached.review_prompt_hint: Does the corrupted state actually cause the claimed loss/DoS?
examples: revert that is caught / has no consequence

detection_hints: duplicate_of set; shares a dispositions finding_ref; dup-map
duplicate_root_cause.required_evidence: a distinct root cause or entrypoint
duplicate_root_cause.review_prompt_hint: Same root cause as another finding? merge.
examples: two findings on the same underflow site

detection_hints: Low/Info impact labeled High; best-practice
severity_overclaim.review_prompt_hint: Is the severity justified by a concrete impact, or is it best-practice?

detection_hints: public entrypoint exists but the precondition/impact is unproven; speculative reachability
needs_runtime_poc.required_evidence: a runtime PoC reaching the precondition state and the impact
needs_runtime_poc.review_prompt_hint: The mechanism is plausible but reachability of the precondition/impact is unproven — a fork PoC is required before confirming.
examples: DS-004 needs the SOP div-by-zero state
RE-001 needs a concrete reentrant exploit
